newsitem.title: USA: Primary sector grabs U.S. corporate bond spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Primary sector grabs U.S. corporate bond spotlight.

text.p: Despite a pickup in corporate bond secondary trading activity on Tuesday, the primary arena continued to grab the spotlight while spreads to U.S. Treasuries closed unchanged, players said.
"We actually had an active day with some buying and selling seen but overall the tone was relatively quiet," said one high-grade trader. "The focus remains on new issues."
Among investment-grade issuers on Tuesday,Sears unit Sears Roebuck Acceptance Corp sold $300 million in A2/A-minus rated five-year notes at 45 basis points over Treasuries.

Donohue Inc unit Donohue Forest Products, issued $200 million in 10-year notes at 95 basis points via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. Donohue is a major Canadian producer of newsprint, market pulp and lumber.
Still, a little over $4.0 billion in investment-grade debt is slated to hit the market, dealers said.

On Wednesday, Norfolk Southern Corp's highly anticipated mega-debt offering is expected to splash down in the new issue market. The deal was launched Tuesday as a $3.65 billion seven-tanche deal which will be underwritten by joint lead managers JP Morgan Securities and Merrill Lynch & Co.
Tranches launched with official price talk are:
--$400 million three-year debt at 35 to 37 basis points
--$500 million five-year debt at 44 to 46 basis points
--$650 million 40-year debt with seven-year put option
at 41 to 44 basis points
--$750 million 10-year debt at 65 to 68 basis points
--$450 million 20-year debt at 75 to 78 basis points
--$650 million 30-year debt at 85 to 88 basis points
--$250 million 100-year debt at 95 to 98 basis points
Initially slated to come as a $3.0 billion four-part deal, the offering was increased in size to meet investor demand.
Players said the supermarket sector continued to perform well.
Smith's Food & Drug Centers 11-1/4 bonds rose another 1/4 point following a four point gain on Monday, traders said.
On Monday, general merchandiser, Fred Meyer Inc announced it would buy the supermarket chain assuming $1.3 billion of Smith's Food debt in the acquisition.
Smith's Food bonds were quoted at 116-5/8 bid, 116-7/8 offer, traders said.
Quality Food paper was also stronger by a 1/4 point, traders said.
Among other supermarket issues, Bruno's Inc paper was quoted up 1/8 at 104-1/2 bid, 105 offer and Pathmark Stores debt also traded up 3/8 at 94-1/2 bid, 94-7/8 offer, traders added.
In the high-yield primary sector among issuers to tap the market were Amphenol Corp with $240 million in B2/B-minus rated 10-year notes at 316.5 basis points over Treasuries.
In addition, Owens-Illinois set $300 million in Ba1/BB-plus seven-year notes at 125 basis points.
